BUS.G12.T3.INSURANCE.A1.title: Investment: insurance & assurance
BUS.G12.T3.INSURANCE.A1.description: Distinguishing assurance from insurance, compulsory and non-compulsory insurance, life insurance and retirement annuities, insurance of goods, the principle of average with over- and under-insurance calculations, and the compulsory funds — the Unemployment Insurance Fund (UIF) and Road Accident Fund (RAF).
BUS.G12.T3.INSURANCE.A1.recovery_strategy: Assurance covers an event that WILL happen (death) — e.g. life cover. Insurance covers an event that MIGHT happen (fire, theft). UIF and RAF are compulsory. Under the principle of average, under-insuring means you are paid out proportionally less.

questions.question: Assurance covers an event that:
options: Will definitely happen, such as death
Might or might not happen, such as a fire
questions.expected: Will definitely happen, such as death
questions.memo: Assurance covers a certain event (such as death); the question is only when it happens, not if.

questions.question: Insurance covers an event that:
options: Might happen, such as fire or theft
Is certain to happen, such as death
questions.expected: Might happen, such as fire or theft
questions.memo: Insurance covers an uncertain event that may or may not happen, such as fire, theft or an accident.

questions.question: The _________ is the compulsory fund that helps workers who lose their jobs.
questions.expected: UIF
questions.memo: The Unemployment Insurance Fund (UIF) is a compulsory fund that provides short-term relief to workers who become unemployed.

questions.question: True or false: The Road Accident Fund (RAF) compensates victims of road accidents.
questions.expected: True
questions.memo: The RAF is a compulsory fund that compensates people injured or affected by road accidents.

questions.question: Life _________ pays out a sum when the insured person dies.
questions.expected: assurance
questions.memo: Life assurance pays out on death — a certain event — which is why it is 'assurance' rather than 'insurance'.

questions.question: True or false: Over-insurance means insuring an item for more than it is worth.
questions.expected: True
questions.memo: Over-insurance is insuring for more than an item's actual value — but a payout is still limited to the real loss, so you cannot profit.

questions.question: Sort each example into assurance or insurance.

items.text: Life cover that pays out on death
Cover against the shop burning down
A retirement annuity that matures at a set age
Cover against a delivery van being stolen
A funeral policy paying out on death
Cover against flood damage to stock

questions.expected: All six items in correct buckets (or ≥75%)
questions.memo: Cover for certain events (death, reaching a set age) is assurance; cover for uncertain events (fire, theft, flood) is insurance.

questions.question: Which of these is COMPULSORY insurance in South Africa?
questions.expected: UIF contributions for employees
questions.memo: UIF (and the RAF levy on fuel) is compulsory; insuring possessions like a TV or pet is voluntary (non-compulsory).

questions.question: An asset worth R100 000 is insured for only R50 000. Under the principle of average, what is paid for a R20 000 loss?
questions.memo: Payout = (insured ÷ value) × loss = (R50 000 ÷ R100 000) × R20 000 = ½ × R20 000 = R10 000.

questions.question: A retirement _________ is a long-term plan that helps a person save for retirement.
questions.expected: annuity
questions.memo: A retirement annuity is a long-term savings plan designed to provide income after retirement.

questions.question: What does under-insurance mean for a claim?
options: The item is insured for less than its value, so the payout is reduced proportionally
The insurer pays double the loss
The item is insured for more than its value
No claim can ever be made
questions.expected: The item is insured for less than its value, so the payout is reduced proportionally
questions.memo: Under-insurance means cover below the item's value, so under the principle of average the payout is scaled down.

questions.question: True or false: Both the UIF and the RAF are compulsory.
questions.expected: True
questions.memo: The UIF (employee contributions) and the RAF (funded by a fuel levy) are both compulsory.

questions.question: Sort each item into compulsory or non-compulsory insurance.
questions.expected: All six items in correct buckets (or ≥75%)
questions.memo: UIF and the RAF levy are compulsory; insuring household goods, a cellphone or taking a voluntary life policy is non-compulsory.

questions.question: If a business over-insures stock worth R30 000 for R45 000 and the stock is destroyed, how much can it claim?
options: R30 000 — the actual value, since you cannot profit from insurance
questions.expected: R30 000 — the actual value, since you cannot profit from insurance
questions.memo: Insurance compensates the actual loss, not more — over-insuring does not let you claim above the item's real value.

questions.question: Why does a business insure its goods and premises?
options: To protect against losses from events like fire, theft or flood
To increase the chance of a fire
To raise the price of its products
questions.expected: To protect against losses from events like fire, theft or flood
questions.memo: Insuring goods and premises protects the business financially if an uncertain event like fire or theft occurs.

questions.question: The principle of _________ reduces a payout when an item is under-insured.
questions.expected: average
questions.memo: The principle of average scales the payout down in proportion to how much the item was under-insured.

questions.question: Equipment worth R200 000 is insured for R150 000. Under the principle of average, what is paid for a R40 000 loss?
A young breadwinner wants to make sure their family is provided for if they die. Which product fits best?
options: Life assurance, which pays out on death
questions.expected: Life assurance, which pays out on death
questions.memo: Because death is certain, life assurance is the product designed to provide for dependants when the breadwinner dies.

questions.question: Why is under-insuring assets a risky decision for a business?
options: The principle of average means a claim will be paid out only in proportion, leaving a shortfall
Under-insurance always pays out the full value
questions.expected: The principle of average means a claim will be paid out only in proportion, leaving a shortfall
questions.memo: If an under-insured asset is damaged, the payout is scaled down, so the business must cover the rest of the loss itself.

questions.question: What is the key difference that decides whether a product is 'assurance' or 'insurance'?
options: Whether the event covered is certain to happen (assurance) or only possible (insurance)
The price of the monthly premium
Whether the company is large or small
The colour of the policy document
questions.expected: Whether the event covered is certain to happen (assurance) or only possible (insurance)
questions.memo: Assurance covers a certain event (like death); insurance covers an uncertain one (like fire or theft) — that certainty is the deciding difference.
